fields.name: Tiger
fields.fun_fact: Tigers love water and are amazing swimmers! And guess what? Every tiger has its own unique stripe pattern!

fields.name: Emperor Penguin
fields.habitat: Antarctica and the surrounding Southern Ocean
fields.fun_fact: Emperor penguin dads keep their eggs warm on their feet! They huddle together in huge groups to stay warm during the freezing Antarctic winter.

fields.name: Komodo Dragon
fields.fun_fact: Komodo dragons are the largest living lizards in the world and can grow up to about 10 feet long! Even with their huge size, they can run surprisingly fast, up to around 12 miles per hour/19 kilometers per hour for short bursts.

fields.name: Cane toad
fields.fun_fact: Cane toads are some of the largest toads in the world and can grow about as big as a dinner plate! They also have special glands behind their eyes that help protect them from predators.

fields.name: Scarlet Skunk Cleaner Shrimp
fields.fun_fact: Why Arthropod? Because shrimp are crustaceans, and crustaceans belong to the arthropod group! Guess what? A shrimp’s heart is in its head area! That’s because its head and chest are joined together.

fields.name: Giant Manta Ray
fields.habitat: tropical, subtropical, and temperate oceanic waters
fields.fun_fact: Manta rays can grow wider than a car! Even though they are huge, they eat tiny plankton by filtering it from the water as they swim.

fields.name: Red Kangaroo
fields.habitat: Open scrublands, grasslands, and desert outback across mainland Australia
fields.fun_fact: When a red kangaroo joey is born, it is blind, hairless, and roughly the size of a jellybean or grape!
